title: Zetwerk Files Updated IPO Papers as FY26 Revenue Hits Rs 15,900 Crore
excerpt: The contract manufacturing unicorn filed its updated DRHP with SEBI, aiming to raise Rs 2,600 crore in fresh capital while reporting a 24% revenue jump in FY26.
body:
• Zetwerk filed its updated DRHP with SEBI on August 14, aiming to raise Rs 2,600 crore ($272 million) in fresh capital through the IPO
  • FY26 revenue from continuing operations reached Rs 15,913 crore, up 24% from Rs 12,800 crore in FY25
  • The company reported a pre-tax loss of Rs 916 crore in FY26 due to one-off charges from exiting its civil infrastructure business
  • Zetwerk operates 20+ manufacturing facilities serving 1,100 customers across more than a dozen countries

Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses filed updated draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) papers with the Securities and Exchange Board of India on August 14, moving closer to what would be one of the larger Indian IPOs in the second half of 2026. The contract manufacturing platform aims to raise Rs 2,600 crore ($272 million) in fresh capital through the issue, alongside an offer for sale of 96.8 million shares by existing investors.

Revenue Rebounds After Strategic Restructuring

The updated filing disclosed FY26 revenue of Rs 15,913 crore from continuing operations, a 24% jump from Rs 12,800 crore in FY25. The FY25 figure itself had declined from Rs 14,443 crore in FY24 as the company exited unprofitable segments and scaled down its civil infrastructure business.

The revenue recovery in FY26 was driven by Zetwerk's strengthened presence across core manufacturing verticals — energy, precision manufacturing, capital goods, and its ecosystem (trading) segment. The company had an order book exceeding Rs 12,000 crore as of March 2026, providing revenue visibility over the next 12-18 months.

CRISIL Ratings, which assigned an A-/Negative rating to Zetwerk's proposed Rs 500 crore non-convertible debentures, estimated the company's operating margin at approximately 2.6% for FY26. The thin margin reflects the nature of contract manufacturing, where high volumes generate substantial revenue but leave limited room for error in execution.

Losses Persist on One-Off Charges

Despite the revenue growth, Zetwerk reported a pre-tax loss of Rs 916 crore in FY26, driven by one-off provisions and charges related to its exit from the civil engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) business. The company had been winding down this segment as part of a strategic decision to focus on higher-margin, technology-driven manufacturing services ahead of the listing.

The CRISIL negative outlook specifically flags the risk of higher-than-expected provisions or losses from the civil EPC exit. In FY25, net losses had already narrowed 60% to Rs 371 crore from Rs 918 crore the prior year, but the FY26 charges pushed the figure back up.

Scale and Client Diversification

Zetwerk now operates more than 20 manufacturing facilities catering to over 1,100 customers across sectors including electronics, energy, capital goods, aerospace, and defence in more than a dozen countries. Its client list includes Schneider Electric, Indian Oil, Siemens, Acer, NTPC Renewable Energy, Nextracker, Samsung India Electronics, National Aluminium Company, and ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India.

Customer concentration remains low, with the top 10 clients contributing only about 30% of FY26 revenue. The company has also expanded inorganically, completing nine acquisitions and joint ventures to date.

IPO Timing and Capital Allocation

Zetwerk plans to use Rs 1,800 crore of the fresh capital raised to repay debt, with the remainder allocated to corporate purposes and potential acquisitions. The public filing comes as India's primary market revives after a muted first half — 22 companies have launched or announced IPOs since July, compared to about 27 public issues across January through June.

The company had earlier filed confidential papers with SEBI in March 2026 and appointed Kotak Mahindra Capital, JM Financial, Avendus Capital, and the Indian units of HSBC, Morgan Stanley, and Goldman Sachs to manage the issue. Zetwerk has raised over $889 million in private funding from investors including Greenoaks, Peak XV Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Accel.

Founded in 2018 by IIT graduates including CEO Amrit Acharya, Zetwerk started as a manufacturing marketplace for industrial goods and has since evolved into a global contract manufacturing operation with a presence across India, the US, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East and Africa.
nri_angle: Zetwerk's global operations across the US, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East, along with its marquee international client base, make it a closely watched IPO for NRI investors tracking India's manufacturing sector.
